name: Coily Hair
description: Coily hair is a texture characterized by tightly coiled strands. It is typically associated with African and Afro-Caribbean descent, but can also be found in other ethnicities.
characteristics: Can have a watermelon seed appearance
recommended_ingredients: Hydrating agents like glycerin, panthenol, and hyaluronic acid
Humectants such as honey, aloe vera, and coconut water
Protein treatments for strength (e.g., keratin, silk protein)
ingredients_to_avoid: Sulfates, which can strip natural oils from the hair
Alcohols that are drying (e.g., SD alcohol)
washing_frequency: Every 2-3 days or as needed, depending on scalp oiliness
oil_recommendation: Use lightweight oils that don't weigh the hair down (e.g., argan, jojoba)

morning_routine.action: Rinse hair with cool water to close cuticles and seal in moisture

night_routine.action: Apply a deep conditioner or leave-in treatment before bedtime
night_routine.purpose: Penetrates the hair shaft to hydrate and repair overnight

weekly_care: Use a clarifying shampoo once a week to remove buildup
Deep condition every 1-2 weeks for optimal moisture retention
deep_conditioning_frequency: Once a week or as needed, depending on hair dryness
heat_styling_recommendation: Minimize heat styling; use heat protectant and allow natural air drying when possible
lifestyle_tips: Eat a balanced diet rich in proteins, vitamins, and minerals
Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water
Protect hair from environmental damage with sun hats or scarves
foods_for_healthy_hair: Proteins like lean meats, fish, and legumes
Fruits and vegetables rich in antioxidants (e.g., berries, leafy greens)
Healthy fats from nuts, seeds, and avocados
common_mistakes: Using too much heat styling tools
Not moisturizing enough or skipping deep conditioning sessions
do: Use a wide-tooth comb to detangle without breaking hair
Apply products while the hair is damp for better absorption
Try microfiber towels or air drying instead of towel rubbing
dont: Skip moisturizing and deep conditioning steps
Overstyle with heat tools, as it can cause breakage
Use heavy oils that can weigh down your coily hair

seasonal_care.summer: Protect hair from sun damage by wearing hats or applying a leave-in UV protectant
seasonal_care.winter: Stay extra hydrated and use hydrating treatments to combat dryness
seasonal_care.monsoon: Increase deep conditioning sessions due to increased humidity

expert_tips: Consistency is key with hair care routines for coily hair
Experiment with different products and techniques to find what works best for your specific needs
